title: Is This Why Science Advances One Funeral at a Time?
titleZh: 科学家的创造力，会随着年龄发生怎样的演变？
summary:
几个世纪以来，科学界长期处于头重脚轻的格局之中。真正能够影响乃至塑造知识走向的，是极少数站在领域顶端的专家。诺贝尔奖由他们摘得。数百万美元、持续数年的科研资助也由他们获得。甚至连学术教科书都因他们而被改写。相比之下，科学界的其他从业者更像是短暂驻足的过客，依附于这些巨人的光环之下。然而，一名研究者的创造力、创新能力与洞察力，在其漫长的科研生涯中究竟会经历怎样的演变？

来源：Nautilus；作者：Bob Grant；原文发布时间：2026-05-13 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: For centuries, science has been a top-heavy enterprise. A vanishingly small number of field-leading experts has the propensity to shape knowledge. They who win the Nobels. They who secure the multi-year, millions-of-dollars grants. They who rewrite the textbooks. Other workers in science are merely passing through, riding the coattails of these giants. But how does a researcher’s capacity for invention, innovation, and insight change over the course of a career in science?
paragraphs.contentZh: 几个世纪以来，科学界长期处于头重脚轻的格局之中。真正能够影响乃至塑造知识走向的，是极少数站在领域顶端的专家。诺贝尔奖由他们摘得。数百万美元、持续数年的科研资助也由他们获得。甚至连学术教科书都因他们而被改写。相比之下，科学界的其他从业者更像是短暂驻足的过客，依附于这些巨人的光环之下。然而，一名研究者的创造力、创新能力与洞察力，在其漫长的科研生涯中究竟会经历怎样的演变？

paragraphs.contentEn: Even the giants seem to have something of a use-by date. In one year of publishing—1905—Albert Einstein turned physics on its head and revolutionized humanity’s understanding of our universe with his concepts of special relativity, mass energy equivalence, the photoelectric effect, and Brownian motion. He was 26 years old. The shockwaves of the ideas contained in four papers continue to ripple through the fabric of spacetime and shape the intellectual evolution of our species. But toward the tail end of Einstein’s life, he argued strenuously against the concepts undergirding the emerging field of quantum mechanics, the ideas that are shaking up physics yet again and may lay bare even more of our universe’s mysteries.
paragraphs.contentZh: 即便是科学巨匠，其创造力似乎也存在某种保质期。仅在1905年这一年，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦接连提出了狭义相对论、质能等价、光电效应和布朗运动这四大理论，彻底颠覆了物理学界，全面革新了人类对宇宙的认知。那一年，他不过26岁。这四篇论文所承载的思想冲击，至今仍如涟漪般在时空的经纬中回荡，塑造着人类这一物种的智识演进。然而到了晚年，爱因斯坦却激烈驳斥那些支撑起量子力学这一新兴领域的核心理念，而正是这些理论，如今再度撼动着物理学，并有望进一步揭示宇宙更深层的奥秘。

paragraphs.contentEn: Historians of science have long debated both the typical shape of a scientist’s output curve and the reasons for its particular slopes, traced throughout the arc of a career in research. Creativity declines with age. Or not. Young scientists are more likely to crack open a field and explore uncharted territory. Older researchers acquire the necessary experience and knowledge necessary to shift paradigms and point inquiry in new directions. And so on.
paragraphs.contentZh: 一名科学家的学术产出曲线通常呈现怎样的形态？而贯穿整个科研生涯的这条轨迹，又为何会出现那些特定的起伏？长期以来，科学史学家始终在讨论这两个问题。有人认为，创造力会随着年龄增长而衰退。但也有人并不认同这种说法。年轻科学家更有可能开辟全新领域，探索无人涉足的未知地带。而年长研究者则积累了必要的经验与知识，更有能力推动范式转变，并为科学探索指引新的方向。类似这样的观点，还有很多。

paragraphs.contentEn: Now, researchers from the universities of Pittsburgh and Chicago have proposed a new model. The key lies in splitting creativity into two separate expressions—novelty through recombining existing insights into new connective ideas and disruptive innovation, the Einsteinian flashes of brilliance that rewrite a field’s trajectory. By analyzing the output of more than 12 million scientists over the course of six decades, from 1960 to 2020, they find that researchers across the world tend to increase their capacity for connective novelty as they age and decrease in their ability to disrupt. They published their findings in Science last week.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如今，匹兹堡大学与芝加哥大学的研究人员提出了一种新的模型。其核心在于将创造力拆解为两种不同的表现维度——一种是融合式创新，即通过重组既有学术见解建立新的关联；另一种是颠覆式创新，即那种如爱因斯坦般的灵感爆发，足以改写整个领域的发展轨迹。通过分析1960年至2020年这60年间超过1200万名科学家的学术产出，研究者发现，随着年龄增长，全球范围内科研人员的融合式创新能力往往逐渐增强，颠覆式创新能力则呈下降趋势。这项研究成果已于上周发表在《科学》期刊上。

paragraphs.contentEn: The authors invoke Douglas Adam’s take on a life spent wandering through the intellectual wilds. “This life-cycle pattern accords with science-fiction author Douglas Adams’ observation about technological change,” they wrote. “What exists at one’s intellectual ‘birth’ feels normal, what appears during early career feels revolutionary, and what emerges after maturity feels suspect.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究作者援引了道格拉斯·亚当斯关于“一生漫游于智识荒野”的洞见。他们在论文中写道：“这一生命周期模式，与科幻作家道格拉斯·亚当斯关于技术变革的论断不谋而合。在一个人的‘智识初生期’，既有的一切都显得稀松平常；在职业生涯早期出现的事物，让人觉得具有革命意义；而进入成熟阶段后涌现的新事物，则往往招致怀疑。”

paragraphs.contentEn: They contend that, as scientists age and their experience deepens, they become attached to the ideas upon which they built their career. This makes replacing this foundation harder as time wears on. But it also makes it more likely that they notice some connection between two or more established, familiar ideas. “Even the greatest minds, such as Einstein, transitioned from disruptor to gatekeeper when quantum mechanics threatened his nostalgic view of the universe,” they wrote.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员指出，随着科学家年龄增长、经验不断累积，他们往往会日益依附于那些支撑其学术生涯建立起来的核心理念。而随着时间推移，要替换这一根基也变得越发困难。但与此同时，这种积累也让他们更有可能在两个或多个既有的熟悉理念之间，发现潜在的关联。他们在论文中写道：“即便是爱因斯坦这样的伟大头脑，在量子力学挑战其深为眷恋的古典宇宙观时，也从一位颠覆者转变为一名守门人。”

paragraphs.contentEn: It was the Nobel laureate and quantum physicist Max Planck who wrote that “science advances one funeral at a time” (which is actually a somewhat artful translation of his original statement, in German) about revered gatekeepers and their nostalgia for insights past that keep leaps in scientific understanding from happening. Turns out, he may have been right.
paragraphs.contentZh: 诺贝尔奖得主、量子物理学家马克斯·普朗克曾写道：“科学的每一次进步，都伴随着一场葬礼”（这句话其实是对他德文原句颇为巧妙的一种意译），他所指向的，是那些备受尊崇的学科守门人以及他们对既有认知的怀旧与执着，正是这种惯性，阻碍着科学理解的跃迁。如今看来，他或许是对的。
